episodes.title: NVIDIA's 11-Name Successor Shortlist, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, GPT-6 Cyber
episodes.about: AI news today: an 11-name shortlist for NVIDIA's next CEO, Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator, and OpenAI's Daybreak cyber tools. The hosts walk through the shortlist - four insiders including Colette Kress and co-founder Chris Malachowsky, and seven outsiders including Pat Gelsinger, Tim Cook and AMD's Lisa Su - and what the next leader could mean for open-weight models. Also covered: United Airlines blocking AI agents like Meta's Muse from completing ticket purchases, ChatGPT Work sending emails it was told not to send, NVIDIA's Groot 2 robotics model, and forensic evidence tying top Chinese AI models to NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
episodes.why: The Friday roundup with two actual launches in it - Gemini 4 Hydrogen and GPT-6 Cyber with its Daybreak tools - plus the 11 names who could replace Jensen Huang.

episodes.title: Washington Is Taking Control of AI
episodes.about: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia is becoming a turning point in Washington's battle over AI and China. NLW examines how the fallout is empowering China hawks, accelerating chip export restrictions, and raising questions that go well beyond the disputed spy allegations. Plus, the competing arguments over selling chips to China - and what new leadership at Nvidia could mean for the financing that keeps the AI boom moving.
episodes.why: Washington is using Huang's exit to push tighter chip export restrictions on China - NLW separates the policy shift from the scandal itself.

episodes.title: Implementing Federated Learning to enhance Agentic AI
episodes.about: How can AI models learn from private data without compromising privacy? Chris Benson is joined by Lorenzo Sani, a research scientist at Flower Labs and PhD researcher at Cambridge, to explore federated learning and privacy-preserving AI. They discuss how collaborative learning can expand access to private data for LLM training, how model trajectories can help improve agentic AI systems, the benefits of open-weight models, and real-world applications of locally hosted AI agents, from healthcare and robotics to everyday automation.
episodes.why: Flower Labs' Lorenzo Sani on training models on private data that never leaves the device - and using model trajectories to improve agentic AI.

episodes.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet and More AI News
episodes.about: Jaeden Schafer explores the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet, enabling users to make purchases securely, as well as Google's new Gemini-powered glasses, available for pre-order. The roundup also covers record chip-company profits, SpaceX's massive AI supercomputing investments, OpenAI and Chinese AI chip export controls, ongoing legal challenges over AI development, and a new AI model from Mirandil.
episodes.why: Sixteen minutes for the ChatGPT Wallet launch and Google's Gemini glasses pre-orders - a news roundup the Jensen story does not lead.

episodes.title: Ep. 4 — The Silent Swap: Gemini 2.5 Auto-Routing, Claude 5.2 Pricing, GPUStack on KEV & vLLM 0.33
episodes.about: On Dec 1, Google starts routing Gemini 2.5 Pro requests to Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Flash to Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite - no error, a different model. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 list at $8 in / $40 out per million tokens (20% below 5.1), and Sonnet 4.5 retires Nov 30. GPUStack CVE-2026-102895 (CVSS 9.8) treats localhost as admin and is on CISA's exploited list - upgrade to 2.2.0. vLLM 0.33.0 fixes a model-config path traversal, and both OpenAI and Anthropic lost their Microsoft 365 connectors to the same upstream outage.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — This Week in AIOps is a new, small ops show (this is episode 4) for people running AI in production: Google will silently swap your Gemini model on Dec 1, and there is a CVSS 9.8 GPUStack flaw to patch first.
